raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Prevent catastrophic backtracking in Poolside v1 and Dots tool-call extraction. This updates the existing PR after upstream drift; it does not introduce another parser or a duplicate fix.

## Claims

- Poolside function names no longer compete with adjacent whitespace quantifiers; names containing internal spaces still parse. Whitespace-only names are intentionally rejected instead of producing an empty function name.
- Dots whitespace runs are possessive while the block capture remains lazy, preserving first-closing-marker and adjacent-block behavior.
- Regex operations use the existing timeout setting, and timeouts take the parser's existing content/no-call fallback.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `173d063acdb499ec2980b3d9561a6fbff0fd3701`. Fresh local tests use the source checkout, real protocol classes and the supported CPU platform:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python -m pytest -q \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_dots_tool_parser.py
# 34 passed in 10.31s, with repository conftests
```

The command ran through `uv run --no-project --python <existing-venv>/bin/python --with orjson`. Ruff 0.14.0 checks and formatting pass on all four files; Python compilation and `git diff --check` pass.

Fresh negative controls use the upstream `ab9f51f101` parser files, which are byte-identical to `173d063acdb` for both affected parsers and their upstream tests:

```bash
pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py \
  -k whitespace_only_tool_call_name_is_rejected
# 1 failed: upstream emits a tool call with an empty name

pytest -q --timeout=6 --timeout-method=signal \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_dots_tool_parser.py \
  -k 'whitespace_padded_tool_call_is_not_quadratic or unterminated_block_with_whitespace_is_not_cubic'
# 2 failed: each unfixed regex exceeds the six-second external watchdog
```

The external watchdog only bounds the negative-control runs; the unchanged five-second assertions run normally and pass on the fixed branch. No watchdog, skip or threshold change is added to the repository.

Targeted mypy 1.20.2 with the hook dependencies checks all four files. It reports the same two upstream `_allowed_types` list-invariance errors on main and this branch (base lines 209/360, branch lines 225/384), with no additional errors. This is not a passing type-check result.

No fresh model, tokenizer-checkpoint, live serving or GPU validation was available. These are parser-level results, not end-to-end throughput measurements. Earlier performance figures in the conversation are historical.

## Details

Poolside's captured name overlapped with surrounding `\s*` runs. Pinning its first and last characters to non-whitespace removes those ambiguous splits. Dots had overlapping whitespace around a lazy DOTALL capture; making only the whitespace possessive keeps the capture ending at the first marker.

The rebase preserves the current `vllm.renderers.chat_utils` import path, custom tool-choice handling and schema-aware value conversion, including nullable-string handling and its upstream tests. The diff remains four files, 188 additions and 10 deletions. No dependency or core-engine changes.

Buildkite's entrypoints API-server-generate step selects `tool_parsers` and depends on the affected paths. Fresh CI is separate from local validation.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Changes stay in the existing parsers and reuse the timeout setting.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Focused tests and base regressions are verified; live serving and checkpoint-dependent validation remain outstanding.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Ruff and diff checks pass; upstream typing errors are documented separately.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, merge resolution, behavior changes, evidence and limitations are recorded.
</details>

```

It only started running because merging `main` brought in upstream docs changes, which made its "docs-affecting files changed" test true — this PR itself touches no docs.

`pre-run-check` is the contributor gate (`'verified'`/`'ready'` label, or 4+ merged PRs — currently 3), so both reds have one cause and neither is about this change. Nothing to fix here.

The merge itself: clean, no conflicts, and none of this PR's files had an upstream change in the window (0 commits each). Tests on the merged head below.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Both conflicts were the same thing, one per parser, and both in the import block: `main` moved `make_tool_call_id` from `vllm.entrypoints.chat_utils` to `vllm.renderers.chat_utils`, so my line importing it from the old location collided with its removal.

The fix itself is untouched: both repaired patterns (`dots`'s possessive `\s*+`, `poolside`'s `[^\s<]` token boundary) and all four `VLLM_TOOL_PARSE_REGEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` call sites are still there, and the PR's contribution against `main` is unchanged at 4 files, +188/-10.

On the merged head: `test_dots_tool_parser.py` + `test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py` → **29 passed**. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

One note on what the regression check does and does not prove, since I would rather state it than imply more: reverting both patterns to their fragile forms fails `test_whitespace_only_tool_call_name_is_rejected` (1 failed | 28 passed). That is the `poolside` behaviour change biting. The two timing tests (`test_unterminated_block_with_whitespace_is_not_cubic`, `test_whitespace_padded_tool_call_is_not_quadratic`) still pass against the fragile patterns here, because this box is fast enough to stay inside their budget — they are a guard against a regression on CI hardware, not a reproduction on every machine. The `dots` change has no behavioural delta at all; the timeout is what bounds it.

> ``Conflict resolved in `2d7b9a775`.``

One upstream commit in that window touched files this PR owns, so here is what it was and how the two sides sit together now:

- `83773ecdf` "[Frontend] Support CustomToolCall in the non-Harmony Responses API (#5…)" — adds `ToolChoiceCustom` to the `openai.types.responses` import and to the `isinstance` check in `PoolsideV1ToolParser.adjust_request`, and adds a `tools=` parameter plus one case to `test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py`. It does not touch either repaired regex or any `timeout=` call site.

On the merged head both sides are present, unmodified:

```
vllm/tool_parsers/poolside_v1_tool_parser.py
  19: from openai.types.responses import ToolChoiceCustom, ToolChoiceFunction   # upstream
  22: import vllm.envs as envs                                                  # this PR
  39: from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import make_tool_call_id                   # upstream path
  85: r"<tool_call>\s*([^\s<](?:[^\n<]*[^\s<])?)\s*"                          # this PR's token boundary
 187: ToolChoiceCustom,                                                         # upstream

vllm/tool_parsers/dots_tool_parser.py
  10: import vllm.envs as envs                                                  # this PR
  24: from vllm.renderers.chat_utils import make_tool_call_id                   # upstream path
  59: rf"{re.escape(tool_call_start_token)}\s*+(.*?)\s*+"                       # this PR's possessive quantifiers
 178-247: timeout=envs.VLLM_TOOL_PARSE_REGEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS                    # this PR
```

To be straight about the evidence: this merge was done through the GitHub merge API rather than a local checkout, so unlike my earlier updates there is **no fresh local test run attached to this head**. The last reported run, on `2d7b9a775`, was 29 passing tests across `tests/tool_parsers/test_dots_tool_parser.py` and `tests/tool_parsers/test_poolside_v1_tool_parser.py`, with `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; the merge added no commit of mine on top of that fix. Say the word and I will attach a run on this head.

The fix is unchanged: 4 files, two repaired patterns, four `VLLM_TOOL_PARSE_REGEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` call sites. Ready for `/ci run` whenever a maintainer has a moment.

Metadata-only force-push on top of the merge above: all eight commits are re-signed under my current identity, `Leizhen Zhang <lzsx618@gmail.com>`, with `Signed-off-by:` updated to match so DCO still passes (it does — DCO is green on this head). New head `590dddb0a1`, was `c9db0c43ce`.

The trees are byte-identical to `c9db0c43ce`, and the merge topology is unchanged: each merge keeps its upstream parent, so no `main` commit was rewritten. Everything in my previous comment — the merge of `main` (`82a24bb82d`), the `83773ecdf` overlap, the two repaired patterns and the four timeout call sites — describes this head unchanged.

Brought up to date with `main` — new head `bebecc4f7`. This branch was **174 commits behind**, which is the state that has had `/ci run` declined before; it is now current.

The merge was clean. One upstream commit had touched `tests/tool_parsers/test_dots_tool_parser.py` since the merge base (`1e330b101`, the mypy follow-imports pass) and it merged without conflict; neither parser source had upstream changes. Diff unchanged at 4 files / +188 −10.

Two things I re-verified on the merged tree rather than assuming:

**1. `VLLM_TOOL_PARSE_REGEX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` still exists** — `vllm/envs.py:245`, default `1`. The `finditer(..., timeout=...)` approach here matches what six other parsers on current `main` already do (`llama`, `pythonic`, `llama4_pythonic`, `lfm2`, `olmo3`, plus this one), so it is not introducing a new convention.

**2. The possessive quantifiers still fix the blowup, and still preserve semantics.** The `dots` block pattern against a start token followed by spaces and no closing tag:

| trailing spaces | `\s*` (main) | `\s*+` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 33 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 400 | 240 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 800 | 1 832 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 1 600 | **timeout > 5 s** | 0.04 ms |

Cost grows ~8× per doubling, i.e. cubic: under `DOTALL` the dot matches a space too, so the two `\s*` runs overlap with the lazy `.*?` between them and a failing match walks every way of splitting the run.

The semantic risk of making those runs possessive is that a block might stop ending at the *first* closing tag. It does not — `.*?` stays lazy:

```
input   <dots_function_call> a </dots_function_call> mid <dots_function_call> b </dots_function_call>
main    ['a', 'b']
this PR ['a', 'b']
```

and a normal single call extracts byte-identically (`{"name": "f", "arguments": {} }` from both).

Ready for `/ci run`.

Brought up to date with `main` — new head `b759db24a`. This branch was **232 commits behind**, which is the state that has had `/ci run` declined before it starts.

The merge is clean and the PR's diff is byte-identical to before it (same four files, same hunks). Upstream touched **none** of those four files in the merged range, so there is no interaction to re-verify; `mypy --python-version 3.11` is clean on all four.

Still blocked only on a maintainer running `/ci run`.

@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
 import json
+import time
 from collections.abc import Iterable
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock
 
@@ -275,3 +276,70 @@ def test_streaming_emits_complete_json_before_end_marker_without_duplication(
         '{"query": "chairs"}'
     )
     assert messages[-1].tool_calls == calls
+
+
+def test_unterminated_block_with_whitespace_is_not_cubic(
+    parser: DotsToolParser,
+) -> None:
+    """A short model output must not take seconds to parse.
+
+    ``_block_regex`` matched ``\\s*(.*?)\\s*`` between the markers. Under
+    ``DOTALL`` a dot matches a space too, so those three quantifiers competed
+    for the same run of spaces and a block with no closing marker after it
+    backtracked through every way of splitting that run: a ~3 KB model output
+    cost more than a minute of CPU on the event loop.
+    """
+    request = _request([_tool("get_weather", {"city": {"type": "string"}})])
+    model_output = DotsToolParser.tool_call_start_token + " " * 4096
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+    assert not result.tools_called
+    assert result.content == model_output
+    # Before the fix this took minutes; a generous bound keeps the test stable
+    # on slow CI machines while still failing on the old behaviour.
+    assert elapsed < 5.0, f"parsing took {elapsed:.1f}s"
+
+
+def test_adjacent_blocks_still_parsed_separately(parser: DotsToolParser) -> None:
+    """The capture must stay lazy: a block ends at the *first* closing marker.
+
+    Guards the fix against a rewrite that lets one block swallow the next.
+    """
+    request = _request([_tool("get_weather", {"city": {"type": "string"}})])
+    block = "{}<invoke name=get_weather><parameter name=city>{}</parameter></invoke>{}"
+    model_output = block.format(
+        DotsToolParser.tool_call_start_token,
+        "Paris",
+        DotsToolParser.tool_call_end_token,
+    ) + block.format(
+        DotsToolParser.tool_call_start_token,
+        "Berlin",
+        DotsToolParser.tool_call_end_token,
+    )
+
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)
+
+    assert result.tools_called
+    assert len(result.tool_calls) == 2
+    assert json.loads(result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {"city": "Paris"}
+    assert json.loads(result.tool_calls[1].function.arguments) == {"city": "Berlin"}
+
+
+def test_whitespace_padded_block_content_is_still_stripped(
+    parser: DotsToolParser,
+) -> None:
+    """Making the whitespace runs possessive must not change what is captured."""
+    request = _request([_tool("get_weather", {"city": {"type": "string"}})])
+    model_output = (
+        DotsToolParser.tool_call_start_token + "\n   <invoke name=get_weather>"
+        "<parameter name=city>Paris</parameter></invoke>   \n"
+        + DotsToolParser.tool_call_end_token
+    )
+
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)
+
+    assert result.tools_called
+    assert json.loads(result.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {"city": "Paris"}

@@ -21,6 +21,7 @@

 import json
+import time
 from typing import Any
 
 import pytest
@@ -388,3 +389,62 @@ def test_nullable_string_keeps_raw_text(raw: str, expected: Any, stream: bool) -
     else:
         calls = parser.extract_tool_calls(output, request).tool_calls
     assert [json.loads(c.function.arguments) for c in calls] == [{"note": expected}]
+
+
+def test_whitespace_padded_tool_call_is_not_quadratic() -> None:
+    """A short model output must not take seconds to parse.
+
+    ``func_detail_regex`` used to allow the captured function name to match
+    whitespace, which overlapped with the ``\\s*`` runs around it. On a block
+    that cannot match, the engine then backtracked through every way of
+    splitting one run of spaces between those quantifiers, so a ~3 KB model
+    output cost more than a minute of CPU on the event loop.
+    """
+    request = _build_weather_request(tool_choice="auto")
+    parser = _make_parser(request)
+
+    # ``<x`` keeps ``func_detail_regex`` from matching, which is what forces
+    # the backtracking; ``func_call_regex`` still yields the block.
+    model_output = "<tool_call>" + " " * 4096 + "<x</tool_call>"
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+    assert not result.tools_called
+    assert result.content == model_output
+    # Before the fix this took >100s; a generous bound keeps the test stable
+    # on slow CI machines while still failing on the old behaviour.
+    assert elapsed < 5.0, f"parsing took {elapsed:.1f}s"
+
+
+def test_whitespace_only_tool_call_name_is_rejected() -> None:
+    """A tool call whose name is only whitespace is skipped, not emitted.
+
+    The previous regex matched here and produced a ``ToolCall`` with an empty
+    function name.
+    """
+    request = _build_weather_request(tool_choice="auto")
+    parser = _make_parser(request)
+
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls("<tool_call>   </tool_call>", request)
+
+    assert not result.tools_called
+    assert result.tool_calls == []
+
+
+def test_function_name_with_internal_whitespace_still_parses() -> None:
+    """Pinning both ends of the name must not break names containing spaces."""
+    request = _build_weather_request(tool_choice="auto")
+    parser = _make_parser(request)
+
+    model_output = (
+        "<tool_call>  get weather  "
+        "<arg_key>city</arg_key><arg_value>Paris</arg_value>"
+        "</tool_call>"
+    )
+
+    result = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request)
+
+    assert result.tools_called
+    assert result.tool_calls[0].function.name == "get weather"

@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@
 
 import regex as re
 
+import vllm.envs as envs
 from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import (
     DeltaFunctionCall,
     DeltaMessage,
@@ -49,8 +50,13 @@ class DotsToolParser(ToolParser):
     tool_call_start_token = "<dots_function_call>"
     tool_call_end_token = "</dots_function_call>"
 
+    # The whitespace runs are possessive. With `\s*` they overlap with the
+    # `.*?` between them -- under `DOTALL` a dot matches a space too -- so a
+    # run of spaces with no closing tag after it can be split between them in
+    # O(n^3) ways and a failing match walks all of them. `.*?` stays lazy so a
+    # block still ends at the *first* closing tag rather than the last.
     _block_regex = re.compile(
-        rf"{re.escape(tool_call_start_token)}\s*(.*?)\s*"
+        rf"{re.escape(tool_call_start_token)}\s*+(.*?)\s*+"
         rf"{re.escape(tool_call_end_token)}",
         re.DOTALL,
     )
@@ -167,7 +173,10 @@ def _parse_xml_invoke(

**2. The possessive quantifiers still fix the blowup, and still preserve semantics.** The `dots` block pattern against a start token followed by spaces and no closing tag:

| trailing spaces | `\s*` (main) | `\s*+` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 33 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 400 | 240 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 800 | 1 832 ms | 0.02 ms |
| 1 600 | **timeout > 5 s** | 0.04 ms |

Cost grows ~8× per doubling, i.e. cubic: under `DOTALL` the dot matches a space too, so the two `\s*` runs overlap with the lazy `.*?` between them and a failing match walks every way of splitting the run.

The semantic risk of making those runs possessive is that a block might stop ending at the *first* closing tag. It does not — `.*?` stays lazy:

```
input   <dots_function_call> a </dots_function_call> mid <dots_function_call> b </dots_function_call>
main    ['a', 'b']
this PR ['a', 'b']
```
